mainTopic: Lessons from תהלים: ברוריה's readings, סמוכין, דוד's five songs of 'ברכי נפשי', and חזקיהו's refusal to stop praying
overview: The גמרא first shows that תהלים chapters 1 and 2 are one chapter, because דוד opened and closed his favorite chapters with אשרי. It then tells two stories about ברוריה. She taught רבי מאיר to pray that sinners do תשובה, not that they die. She also answered a מין who mocked a פסוק about a barren woman. רבי אבהו answers another מין about the order of chapters in תהלים by using סמוכין, passages placed side by side. Next, רבי יוחנן teaches that דוד praised ה׳ with 'ברכי נפשי' in five stages of life, from the womb to the day of death. A second explanation says the five 'ברכי נפשי' match five ways the soul is like הקדוש ברוך הוא. The amud ends with the story of ה׳ making peace between חזקיהו and ישעיהו through חזקיהו's illness. When ישעיהו says the decree is final, חזקיהו insists that a person must never stop praying for mercy, even with a sword on his neck.

steps.title: דוד opened and closed his favorite chapters with 'Happy is'
steps.stepSummary: Every chapter dear to דוד begins and ends with אשרי. Chapter 1 begins 'אשרי האיש' and chapter 2 ends 'אשרי כל חוסי בו', so the two are really one chapter.
steps.simpleTranslation: Every chapter that דוד loved, he began with 'Happy is' and ended with 'Happy is.' He began with 'Happy is' in 'Happy is the man.' He ended with 'Happy is' in 'Happy are all who take refuge in Him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a pattern from דוד's writing to prove that תהלים chapters 1 and 2 are really one chapter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אשרי opens chapter 1 and closes chapter 2. Since דוד framed his beloved chapters this way, the two chapters together form one unit with a matching opening and ending.

keyTerms.meaning: A chapter or section of text

steps.whatToRemember: Chapters 1 and 2 of תהלים count as one chapter, because אשרי opens the first and closes the second.

phrases.aramaic: כָּל פָּרָשָׁה שֶׁהָיְתָה חֲבִיבָה עַל דָּוִד,
phrases.english: Every chapter that was dear to David,
he opened it with "Happy is"
and he closed it with "Happy is."
He opened with "Happy is," as it is written: "Happy is the man."

phrases.aramaic: וְסִייֵּם בְּ״אַשְׁרֵי״, דִּכְתִיב: ״אַשְׁרֵי כָּל חוֹסֵי בוֹ״.
phrases.english: And he closed with "Happy is," as it is written: "Happy are all who take refuge in Him."
phrases.notes: תהלים 2:12. This is the end of the second chapter, so the two chapters are treated as one.

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּל פָּרָשָׁה שֶׁהָיְתָה חֲבִיבָה עַל דָּוִד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the earlier discussion of how the chapters of תהלים are divided.
steps.raayaObject: That תהלים chapters 1 and 2 are a single chapter
steps.raayaSupportSource: The repeated word אשרי at the start of chapter 1 and the end of chapter 2

steps.title: רבי מאיר prays that the thugs who bothered him would die
steps.stepSummary: Thugs in רבי מאיר's neighborhood caused him great pain, so he prayed that they would die.
steps.simpleTranslation: There were some thugs in רבי מאיר's neighborhood who caused him a lot of pain. רבי מאיר was praying about them, asking that they should die.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story. It sets up the problem that ברוריה will respond to next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's prayer is the starting point the rest of the story will question. So far we only know what he did, not why it might be wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: They were causing pain or distress

phrases.english: There were these thugs
who were in Rabbi Meir's neighborhood
and they were causing him a lot of pain.

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה קָא בָּעֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר רַחֲמֵי עִלָּוַיְהוּ
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir was praying about them
so that they would die.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנְהוּ בִּרְיוֹנֵי דַּהֲווֹ בְּשִׁבָבוּתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story, connected to the earlier discussion of how we should view the downfall of the wicked.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר prayed for the death of the thugs who were tormenting him.

steps.title: ברוריה: the verse says 'sins,' not 'sinners'
steps.stepSummary: ברוריה guesses that רבי מאיר relies on 'יתמו חטאים' and points out that the פסוק says sins should end, not sinners.
steps.simpleTranslation: ברוריה, his wife, said to him: What are you thinking? Is it because it is written 'Let sins cease'? Does it say 'sinners'? It says 'sins'!
steps.whatsHappening: ברוריה challenges her husband's prayer by looking closely at the exact word in the פסוק he is probably relying on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could seem to support praying for the wicked to be destroyed. ברוריה notes that the word is חטאים (sins), not חוטאים (sinners). So what should end is the sin, not the people.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it written...? (a way of saying it is not)

phrases.english: Beruria, his wife, said to him:
What are you thinking?
Is it because it is written "Let sins cease"?
Does it say "sinners"?
It says "sins"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי מאיר's prayer from step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's assumed basis for praying for the thugs' death
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק's wording says sins should end, not sinners, so it does not support praying for people to die.

steps.title: ברוריה's second point: the end of the verse
steps.stepSummary: ברוריה adds a proof from the end of the פסוק. If 'sins cease' meant the sinners die, the words 'and the wicked will be no more' would add nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And also, look down at the end of the פסוק: 'and the wicked will be no more.' If 'sins cease' means the sinners die, why add 'the wicked will be no more'?
steps.whatsHappening: ברוריה gives a second argument against her husband's reading, this time from how the פסוק ends.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the first half already meant the sinners are destroyed, the second half would just repeat it. So the first half must mean something else: the sins stop, and then the wicked are no longer wicked.

phrases.english: And also, look down at the end of the verse:
"and the wicked will be no more."
Once "sins cease"
would you need "and the wicked will be no more"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second proof to the challenge in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading 'יתמו חטאים' as the death of sinners
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That reading makes the end of the פסוק repeat the first half for no reason.

steps.title: ברוריה's advice: pray that they do תשובה
steps.stepSummary: ברוריה tells רבי מאיר to pray that the thugs do תשובה. Then 'the wicked will be no more,' because they will no longer be wicked.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, pray for them that they should do תשובה. Then 'the wicked will be no more.'
steps.whatsHappening: After showing what the פסוק does not mean, ברוריה explains what it does mean and what he should pray for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this reading, each half of the פסוק says something real. The sins stop, and as a result the wicked are gone because they have become good people, not because they died.
steps.confusionAlert: 'The wicked will be no more' does not mean they will be killed. It means that after תשובה they will no longer be wicked.

phrases.english: Rather, pray for them
that they should return in repentance,
and then "the wicked will be no more."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בְּעִי רַחֲמֵי עִלָּוַיְהוּ דְּלַהְדְּרוּ בִּתְשׁוּבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the correct reading of the פסוק after the challenges in steps 3 and 4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק calls for the wicked to be destroyed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק calls for sins to end through תשובה, so that the wicked stop being wicked.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches a lasting lesson about prayer: we hope for sinners to change, not for them to be destroyed.

steps.title: רבי מאיר prays and the thugs repent
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר accepted ברוריה's words and prayed for the thugs to do תשובה, and they did.
steps.simpleTranslation: He prayed for them, and they did תשובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends. רבי מאיר follows his wife's advice, and his prayer works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By acting on her words, רבי מאיר shows that he agreed with ברוריה. The happy ending confirms that her reading of the פסוק was correct.
steps.whatToRemember: The right prayer for people who do wrong is that they do תשובה. When רבי מאיר prayed this way, it worked.

phrases.english: He prayed for them,
and they repented.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows רבי מאיר acting on ברוריה's advice from step 5.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Praying for sinners to do תשובה is the proper approach, and here it brought them to repent.

steps.title: A heretic mocks the verse telling a barren woman to sing
steps.stepSummary: A מין asks ברוריה why the פסוק in ישעיהו tells a barren woman to sing just because she never had children.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain heretic said to ברוריה: It is written, 'Sing, barren woman who has not given birth.' Because she has not given birth, she should sing?
steps.whatsHappening: A new story begins. A מין (heretic) attacks a פסוק by asking why being childless should be a reason to sing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not having children is normally a cause of sadness, so the פסוק seems to make no sense. The מין is mocking the פסוק, not sincerely asking. This sets up ברוריה's answer in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: A heretic, someone who rejects the Torah's teachings
A barren woman, one who cannot have children

phrases.english: A certain heretic said to Berurya:
It is written: "Sing, barren woman who has not given birth"
Because she has not given birth, she should sing?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story about ברוריה, following the story where she taught רבי מאיר how to read a פסוק correctly.
steps.kashyaTarget: The פסוק 'רני עקרה לא ילדה' in ישעיהו
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Being childless is a sorrow, so telling a barren woman to sing because of it seems senseless.

steps.title: ברוריה tells the מין to read the end of the verse
steps.stepSummary: ברוריה calls the מין a fool and points him to the end of the פסוק, which says the children of the desolate woman will be many.
steps.simpleTranslation: She said to him: Fool! Look down at the end of the verse, where it is written: 'For more are the children of the desolate than the children of the married wife, said ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: ברוריה pushes back on the question by showing that the מין only read half the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The end of the פסוק talks about the 'desolate' woman having many children. So the פסוק cannot simply be praising childlessness. This prepares her real explanation in the next step.

phrases.english: She said to him: Fool!
Go down to the end of the verse,
as it is written: "For more are the children of the desolate
than the children of the married wife, said the Lord."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the מין's half-reading of the פסוק by bringing in its ending.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The מין's assumption that the פסוק praises being childless
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: He ignored the end of the פסוק, which promises the 'desolate' woman many children.

steps.title: The barren woman is the Jewish people, who bore no children for גיהנם
steps.stepSummary: ברוריה explains that the 'barren woman' is כנסת ישראל, which never gave birth to children destined for גיהנם like the מין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what does 'barren woman who has not given birth' mean? Sing, congregation of Israel, which is like a barren woman who did not give birth to children for גיהנם like you.
steps.whatsHappening: ברוריה gives the true meaning of the פסוק and turns the question back on the מין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'barren woman' is a picture of כנסת ישראל, and 'did not give birth' means she did not produce children headed for גיהנם. That is a real reason to sing. The words 'like you' are a sharp jab: the מין himself is the kind of child Israel did not produce.

keyTerms.meaning: The congregation of Israel, the Jewish people as a whole
The place of punishment for the wicked

steps.whatToRemember: ברוריה twice shows the same skill: read the whole פסוק carefully, and the true meaning appears. The barren woman sings because she had no children for גיהנם.

phrases.english: Rather, what is "barren woman who has not given birth"?
Sing, congregation of Israel,
which is like a barren woman
who did not give birth to children for Gehenna like you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After pointing to the end of the פסוק, ברוריה now explains the beginning correctly.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק praises a woman for simply having no children.
steps.terutzMaskana: The barren woman is כנסת ישראל, rejoicing that she produced no children destined for גיהנם.

steps.title: Why is the אבשלום psalm placed before the שאול psalm
steps.stepSummary: A מין asks רבי אבהו why the chapter about דוד fleeing from אבשלום comes before the chapter about fleeing from שאול, since the שאול story happened first.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain מין said to רבי אבהו: It is written, 'A Psalm of דוד, when he fled from אבשלום his son,' and it is written, 'Of דוד, a מכתם, when he fled from שאול in the cave.' Which event happened first? Since the שאול event happened first, it should have been written first.
steps.whatsHappening: A new story begins. A מין challenges the order of chapters in תהלים, setting up רבי אבהו's answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fleeing from שאול happened years before fleeing from אבשלום. Yet the אבשלום psalm is chapter 3 and the שאול psalm is chapter 57. The מין argues that the book is out of order.

keyTerms.meaning: A type of psalm named in some headings of תהלים

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָהוּא מִינָא לְרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ,
phrases.english: A certain heretic said to Rabbi Abbahu:
It is written: "A Psalm of David,
when he fled from Absalom his son,"
and it is written: "Of David, a mikhtam,
when he fled from Saul in the cave."
Which event happened first?
Since the event of Saul happened first,
let it be written first.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָהוּא מִינָא לְרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another story of a מין challenging a פסוק, this time about the order of chapters in תהלים.
steps.kashyaTarget: The order of chapters 3 and 57 in תהלים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The שאול event came first in time, so its psalm should come first in the book, but it comes later.

steps.title: We learn from passages placed side by side
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו tells the מין that the question only bothers people who do not learn from סמוכין.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: For you, who don't learn lessons from passages placed next to each other, it's a problem. For us, who do learn from them, it's not a problem.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers the מין's question from Step 10 about why the אבשלום chapter comes before the שאול chapter. He says the order is not about time. It is about which passage sits next to which.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מין assumed the chapters should be in time order. רבי אבהו changes the question: the chapter was placed where it is in order to sit next to another chapter, and that placement teaches a lesson. He has not yet said what the lesson is. The גמרא will first prove the method and then explain it.

keyTerms.meaning: Passages placed next to each other in the text, from which a lesson is learned
We explain the text and learn lessons from it

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רבי אבהו answering the מין from the last step.

phrases.aramaic: אַתּוּן דְּלָא דָּרְשִׁיתוּן סְמוּכִין — קַשְׁיָא לְכוּ,
phrases.english: You, who do not learn from juxtaposed passages — it is difficult for you;

phrases.aramaic: אֲנַן דְּדָרְשִׁינַן סְמוּכִים — לָא קַשְׁיָא לַן.
phrases.english: we, who do learn from juxtaposed passages — it is not difficult for us.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַתּוּן דְּלָא דָּרְשִׁיתוּן סְמוּכִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the מין's question from Step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing: the order of the chapters is set by which chapter sits next to which, not by time
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Chapters must appear in the order the events happened
steps.terutzMaskana: The placement is meant to teach a lesson through juxtaposition

steps.title: The source in a פסוק for learning from juxtaposition
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן proves from a פסוק in תהלים that learning from סמוכין is a real method.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יוחנן said: Where do we learn the method of juxtaposition from Scripture? As it says: 'They are joined together forever and ever, made in truth and uprightness.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רבי אבהו's method. It shows that learning from סמוכין comes from a פסוק and is not just a creative idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'סמוכים' (joined, adjoining) in the פסוק describes ה׳'s commands as deliberately placed next to each other. So their placement carries meaning, and we are allowed to learn from it.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
From where in Scripture do we learn juxtaposition?
As it is said: “Joined together forever and ever,”
“made in truth and uprightness.”

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: סְמוּכִין מִן הַתּוֹרָה מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a source in a פסוק for the method רבי אבהו relied on
steps.raayaObject: The legitimacy of learning from סמוכין

steps.title: Why the אבשלום chapter sits next to the גוג ומגוג chapter
steps.stepSummary: The lesson: just as a son really did rebel against his father, people can really rebel against ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why was the chapter of אבשלום placed next to the chapter of גוג ומגוג? So that if someone says to you, 'Is there such a thing as a servant who rebels against his master?', you can answer him, 'Is there such a thing as a son who rebels against his father? Yet it happened, so here too it can happen.'
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא gives the actual lesson of the juxtaposition. This is the full answer to the מין's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The chapter about גוג ומגוג describes nations rising against ה׳, and someone might say that is impossible. The אבשלום story right next to it shows that something just as 'unthinkable', a son rebelling against his own father, really happened. So the war against ה׳ is believable too.

keyTerms.meaning: A chapter or section of text
The nations who will wage the great war in the future
Is there really such a thing?

steps.whatToRemember: The order of the chapters in תהלים teaches a lesson: אבשלום's rebellion proves that even rebellion against ה׳ is possible.

phrases.english: Why was the chapter of Absalom placed next to
the chapter of Gog and Magog?
phrases.notes: That is תהלים 2, 'Why are the nations in an uproar,' right before the אבשלום chapter.

phrases.english: So that if a person should say to you:
Is there a servant who rebels against his master?!
phrases.notes: He means: could anyone really rebel against ה׳?

phrases.english: You too say to him:
Is there a son who rebels against his father?
Yet it happened; here too it can happen.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָמָּה נִסְמְכָה פָּרָשַׁת אַבְשָׁלוֹם לְפָרָשַׁת גּוֹג וּמָגוֹג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the method proven in Step 12 to spell out the lesson promised in Step 11
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the lesson taught by the juxtaposed chapters
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The chapter order looks wrong because it does not follow the timeline
steps.terutzMaskana: אבשלום is placed next to גוג ומגוג to show that rebellion against ה׳ is possible

steps.title: About whom did שלמה say 'She opens her mouth with wisdom'?
steps.stepSummary: A new teaching: רבי יוחנן in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי asks whom a פסוק in משלי is describing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי: What is the meaning of the פסוק 'She opens her mouth with wisdom, and the teaching of kindness is on her tongue'? About whom did שלמה say this פסוק?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new teaching about a different פסוק. This line sets up the question, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק praises someone whose mouth speaks wisdom and kindness. רבי יוחנן wants to know which real person שלמה had in mind.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai:
What is the meaning of what is written:
“She opens her mouth with wisdom,”
“and the teaching of kindness is on her tongue”?

phrases.aramaic: כְּנֶגֶד מִי אָמַר שְׁלֹמֹה מִקְרָא זֶה?
phrases.english: About whom did Solomon say this verse?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי. מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching, unrelated to the מין exchange
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which person the פסוק in משלי 31:26 refers to

steps.title: It refers to דוד, who lived in five worlds and sang
steps.stepSummary: שלמה said the פסוק about his father דוד, who lived through five stages and sang praise in each.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said it only about his father דוד, who lived in five worlds and said a song of praise.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer to Step 14: the person whose mouth spoke wisdom is דוד. This also sets up the next part, where the גמרא will spell out the five 'worlds'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דוד is the example because he sang praise to ה׳ in every stage of his existence. The 'five worlds' are named here but not yet explained.

keyTerms.meaning: Worlds; here meaning stages of existence
A song of praise to ה׳

phrases.aramaic: לֹא אֲמָרוֹ אֶלָּא כְּנֶגֶד דָּוִד אָבִיו,
phrases.english: He said it only about David, his father,
who lived in five worlds,
phrases.notes: Think of these as five stages of life; the גמרא will list them next.

phrases.english: and said a song of praise.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא אֲמָרוֹ אֶלָּא כְּנֶגֶד דָּוִד אָבִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 14
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק refers to דוד, who sang praise in five stages of existence

steps.title: Stage one: דוד sang in his mother's womb
steps.stepSummary: The first of דוד's five stages: while still inside his mother, he sang praise, as shown by a פסוק in תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He lived inside his mother's womb and sang a song of praise, as it says: 'Bless ה׳, O my soul, and all that is within me, His holy name.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts listing the five stages of דוד's life that were mentioned in the last step. The first stage is the womb, and it brings a פסוק to show he praised ה׳ there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'all that is within me' are read as pointing to the inside of his mother, the place where he lived first. So the פסוק becomes proof that דוד praised ה׳ even before he was born.

keyTerms.meaning: as it is said, introducing a פסוק
my insides, all that is within me

phrases.english: He lived in his mother's womb
and said a song,
as it is said:
"Bless ה׳, O my soul,
and all that is within me, His holy name."
phrases.notes: תהלים 103:1. The words 'all that is within me' are what tie this פסוק to the womb.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּר בִּמְעֵי אִמּוֹ וְאָמַר שִׁירָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts spelling out the five stages that step 15 mentioned only in general.
steps.raayaObject: That דוד sang praise while in the womb

steps.title: Stage two: דוד sang when he was born and saw the stars
steps.stepSummary: The second stage: once born, דוד looked at the stars and constellations and praised ה׳, using a פסוק about angels and ה׳'s hosts.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came out into the world, looked at the stars and constellations, and sang a song, as it says: 'Bless ה׳, His angels, mighty in strength, who do His word, listening to the voice of His word; bless ה׳, all His hosts.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second stage, birth. Seeing the stars, דוד praised ה׳, and a פסוק from later in the same chapter is brought as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new detail here is what he saw: the heavens. The פסוק talks about ה׳'s angels and 'hosts' who carry out His word, which fits a praise sung while looking at all of creation above.

keyTerms.meaning: the air of the world, meaning being born

phrases.english: He came out into the air of the world
and looked at the stars and constellations
and said a song, as it is said:
"Bless ה׳, His angels, mighty in strength,
who do His word, listening to the voice of His word;
bless ה׳, all His hosts, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: יָצָא לַאֲוִיר הָעוֹלָם וְנִסְתַּכֵּל בְּכוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת וְאָמַר שִׁירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list with the second of the five stages.
steps.raayaObject: That דוד sang praise when he was born and saw the heavens
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים 103:20–21, 'ברכו ה׳ מלאכיו... ברכו ה׳ כל צבאיו'

steps.title: Stage three: דוד sang while nursing
steps.stepSummary: The third stage: as a nursing baby, דוד looked at his mother's bosom and praised ה׳, using the פסוק 'do not forget all His kindnesses.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He nursed from his mother, looked at her bosom, and sang a song, as it says: 'Bless ה׳, O my soul, and do not forget all His kindnesses.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the third stage, nursing, and brings another פסוק from the same chapter as proof that דוד praised ה׳ then too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key word in the פסוק is גמוליו, which sounds like the word for a nursing or weaning baby. That sound link is why this פסוק fits the nursing stage, and it sets up the question in the next step.

phrases.english: He nursed from his mother's breasts
and looked at her bosom
and said a song, as it is said:
"Bless ה׳, O my soul,
and do not forget all His kindnesses."
phrases.notes: תהלים 103:2. גמוליו sounds like גמולי חלב, a baby being weaned from milk, which is how it connects to nursing.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָנַק מִשְּׁדֵי אִמּוֹ וְנִסְתַּכֵּל בְּדַדֶּיהָ וְאָמַר שִׁירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list with the third of the five stages.
steps.raayaObject: That דוד sang praise while nursing

steps.title: What does 'all His kindnesses' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pauses to ask what special kindness the פסוק means by 'all His kindnesses' in the nursing stage.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by 'all His kindnesses'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask about the words of the last פסוק. This sets up רבי אבהו's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Simply feeding a baby does not seem to explain the special word 'all His kindnesses.' The גמרא wants to know what exact kindness דוד noticed that made him sing.

keyTerms.meaning: what is, what does it mean
babies weaned from milk, the word that sounds like גמוליו

phrases.english: What is "all His kindnesses"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of a phrase in the פסוק quoted in step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What specific kindness of ה׳ the phrase 'כל גמוליו' refers to

steps.title: רבי אבהו: the breasts were placed by the seat of understanding
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו explains that the kindness is that ה׳ placed a mother's breasts in the 'place of understanding,' near the heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: That ה׳ made her breasts in the place of understanding.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers the question from the last step. The special kindness is where ה׳ placed the mother's breasts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'place of understanding' means the heart, so the breasts are near it. That is the specific kindness דוד praised in the nursing stage, not just the fact that he was fed.

keyTerms.meaning: the place of understanding, meaning the heart

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
That He made her breasts
in the place of understanding.
phrases.notes: The 'place of understanding' means the heart, so her breasts are placed near it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: שֶׁעָשָׂה לָהּ דַּדִּים בִּמְקוֹם בִּינָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The kindness is that ה׳ placed the mother's breasts in the place of understanding, near the heart.

steps.title: Why place the breasts near the heart?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבי אבהו's point that the breasts are near the heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why ה׳ placed the breasts near the heart and not somewhere else. This sets up two answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבהו told us where the breasts are and called it a kindness. Now the גמרא wants to know what makes that location a kindness. The question only makes sense if we keep step 20 in mind.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: He means: why did ה׳ put the breasts near the heart, as רבי אבהו just said?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind רבי אבהו's explanation in step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why placing the breasts near the heart is a kindness to the baby.

steps.title: רב יהודה's reason: modesty
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says the purpose is that the nursing baby will not look at the mother's private area.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: so that he will not look at a place of nakedness.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the question. The breasts are high up so the baby will not be looking at the mother's private area while he nurses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Animals usually nurse from the lower body, close to the private area. For humans, ה׳ moved the place of nursing up, so the baby's eyes stay away from ערוה. In this view the kindness is about modesty.

keyTerms.meaning: the private area, a place of nakedness

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
So that he will not look at a place of nakedness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The breasts are placed high so the baby does not look at the mother's private area.

steps.title: רב מתנא's reason: cleanliness
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנא gives a different reason: so the baby will not nurse from a dirty place.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מתנא said: so that he will not nurse from a place of filth.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מתנא gives a second answer to the same question. He says the kindness is that the baby nurses from a clean place, far from where the body gets rid of waste.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה's reason was about what the baby sees. רב מתנא's reason is about where the baby's food comes from. Both agree that the high position is a kindness. They only differ in what the kindness protects the baby from.

keyTerms.meaning: a place of filth or dirt

phrases.english: Rav Mattana said:
So that he will not nurse from a place of filth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 21's question, different from רב יהודה's.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The breasts are placed high so the baby does not nurse from an unclean area of the body.

steps.title: Fourth stage: דוד sees the downfall of the wicked
steps.stepSummary: The fourth stage: דוד saw the wicked fall and sang praise, as shown by a פסוק in תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He saw the downfall of the wicked and sang a song, as it says: 'Let sins cease from the earth, and let the wicked be no more; bless ה׳, my soul, הללויה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the list of דוד's five stages and brings the fourth one. When he saw the wicked fall, he praised ה׳, and a פסוק is brought as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is that the same פסוק that talks about the wicked disappearing ends with 'ברכי נפשי את ה׳.' That ending connects the event to דוד's song of praise. So this stage also fits the pattern of 'ברכי נפשי' that runs through all five stages.

keyTerms.meaning: let them come to an end, be finished

phrases.english: He saw the downfall of the wicked,
and he said a song, as it says:
"Let sins cease from the earth,"
"and the wicked be no more;"
"Bless ה׳, O my soul, Halleluyah."

steps.triggerLanguage: רָאָה בְּמַפַּלְתָּן שֶׁל רְשָׁעִים וְאָמַר שִׁירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side point about nursing and goes back to the list of דוד's five stages.
steps.raayaObject: That דוד sang praise when he saw the wicked fall.
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים 104:35, where the end of the wicked is followed by 'ברכי נפשי את ה׳'.

steps.title: Fifth stage: דוד looks at the day of death
steps.stepSummary: The fifth stage: דוד looked at the day of death and still sang praise, as shown by the opening פסוק of תהלים 104.
steps.simpleTranslation: He looked at the day of death and sang a song, as it says: 'Bless ה׳, my soul; ה׳ my God, You are very great; You are clothed in glory and majesty.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the last of the five stages. Even when דוד thought about the day of death, he praised ה׳.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the most surprising stage, because death does not seem like a reason to sing. The פסוק brought here does not say the word 'death.' The next step asks about this, and step 27 answers it.

phrases.english: He looked at the day of death,
and he said a song, as it says:
"Bless ה׳, O my soul;"
"ה׳ my God, You are very great;"
"You are clothed in glory and majesty."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list with the fifth and final stage.
steps.raayaObject: That דוד sang praise when he looked at the day of death.

steps.title: How do we know this verse is about death?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know the פסוק just quoted is talking about the day of death.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we see that this was said about the day of death?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that the פסוק in step 25 never mentions death. It asks what shows that the פסוק is connected to the day of death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק only praises ה׳'s greatness, glory and majesty. Nothing in it mentions dying. The גמרא wants a textual link before it accepts the claim.

keyTerms.meaning: from where is it shown? what tells us?

phrases.english: From where is it shown
that it was said about the day of death?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי מַשְׁמַע דְּעַל יוֹם הַמִּיתָה נֶאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the proof-text that step 25 used.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What links תהלים 104:1 to the day of death.

steps.title: Proof from the end of the same chapter
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב שילא answers that the end of that same section of תהלים clearly talks about death.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב שילא said: from the end of the passage, as it is written: 'You hide Your face, they are terrified; You take back their breath, they die, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר רב שילא answers the question. Later in the same chapter, the פסוקים talk about ה׳ taking away the breath of living things. That shows the whole chapter, including its opening praise, has death in view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We read the first פסוק in light of the whole passage it belongs to. The ending speaks openly about creatures dying, so the 'ברכי נפשי' at the start is also about death. This completes the fifth stage and the full list of five.

keyTerms.meaning: the end of the passage or topic

steps.whatToRemember: דוד praised ה׳ in five stages of life: in the womb, at birth, while nursing, at the downfall of the wicked, and at the day of death. Each stage is tied to 'ברכי נפשי את ה׳.' The death stage is proven from the end of תהלים 104.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Sheila said:
From the end of the passage, as it is written:
phrases.notes: He means later on in the same chapter, תהלים 104.

phrases.english: "You hide Your face, they are terrified;"
"You take back their breath, they die, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב שֵׁילָא מִסֵּיפָא דְעִנְיָינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 26 and completes the fifth stage.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The end of תהלים 104 speaks of ה׳ taking creatures' breath so they die. That shows the chapter's opening praise is about the day of death.

steps.title: Background of the story and the question on ברכי נפשי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces רב שימי בר עוקבא and רבי שמעון בן פזי, and a question is asked about the meaning of 'ברכי נפשי את ה׳'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי בר עוקבא (some say מר עוקבא) used to spend time with רבי שמעון בן פזי, who arranged אגדה before רבי יהושע בן לוי. He asked him: what does the פסוק 'Bless the Lord, my soul, and all that is within me, His holy name' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a new story and a new question about the same פסוק דוד said, 'ברכי נפשי'. This is a setup for the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא explained the five 'ברכי נפשי' as five stages in דוד's life. Now a different discussion of the same words begins. The questioner wants to know what the words of the פסוק are really about.

keyTerms.meaning: was often found before him (spent time learning with him)
what is the meaning of what is written

phrases.english: Rav Shimi bar Ukva
and some say Mar Ukva,

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה שְׁכִיחַ קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן פַּזִּי,
phrases.english: was often found before Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi,
and he would arrange the aggada
phrases.notes: The 'he' here seems to be רבי שמעון בן פזי, the expert in אגדה.

phrases.english: before Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi.
He said to him: What is that which is written,
"Bless the Lord, my soul,
and all that is within me, His holy name"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion of 'ברכי נפשי', separate from the five stages of דוד's life discussed before.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the פסוק 'ברכי נפשי את ה׳ וכל קרבי את שם קדשו' talking about?

steps.title: A human artist compared to הקדוש ברוך הוא
steps.stepSummary: A person can draw a form on a wall but cannot put life into it. הקדוש ברוך הוא forms a child inside its mother and gives it a soul and insides.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and see: הקדוש ברוך הוא is not like a human being. A human draws a picture on a wall but cannot put breath, a soul, or insides into it. הקדוש ברוך הוא forms a form inside a form (a baby inside its mother) and puts breath, a soul, and insides into it.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer explains that the פסוק praises הקדוש ברוך הוא for creating a living person inside the mother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'כל קרבי' (all my insides) are the key. A human artist can only make an outside picture on a flat wall. הקדוש ברוך הוא makes a full, living being with insides, hidden inside another body, so the person's insides themselves should praise Him.

keyTerms.meaning: the way of flesh and blood (human beings)
a form inside a form (a baby inside its mother)

phrases.english: He said to him: Come and see
that not like the way of the Holy One, Blessed be He,
is the way of flesh and blood.
The way of flesh and blood:
he shapes a form on a wall,
and he cannot put into it
breath and a soul, insides and intestines.
But the Holy One, Blessed be He, is not so;
He shapes a form inside a form
and puts into it breath and a soul,
insides and intestines.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בֹּא וּרְאֵה שֶׁלֹּא כְּמִדַּת הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מִדַּת בָּשָׂר וָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the meaning of 'ברכי נפשי'.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק praises הקדוש ברוך הוא, who, unlike a human artist, forms a living person with a soul and insides inside its mother.

steps.title: חנה's words support this idea
steps.stepSummary: The idea that הקדוש ברוך הוא is the greatest artist matches what חנה said in her song.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what חנה said: 'There is none holy like the Lord, for there is none besides You, and there is no rock like our God.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק from חנה's song to support the idea that הקדוש ברוך הוא is the greatest maker of forms.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חנה said this after the birth of שמואל, so her words fit the theme of forming a child. The next steps will explain two words in her פסוק to show exactly how they support the idea.

keyTerms.meaning: and this is what (someone) said, used to show a match with a source

phrases.english: And this is what Hannah said:
"There is none holy like the Lord,
for there is none besides You,
and there is no rock like our God."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer about הקדוש ברוך הוא as the perfect artist.
steps.raayaObject: That הקדוש ברוך הוא forms living people in a way no human can.

steps.title: צור means artist
steps.stepSummary: The word צור (rock) in חנה's פסוק is read as צייר (artist).
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'there is no rock like our God' mean? There is no artist like our God.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the word צור in חנה's פסוק, showing how it connects to the idea of הקדוש ברוך הוא as an artist.
steps.deeperAnalysis: צור and צייר share the same root letters, like צר צורה (shapes a form) in the previous step. So 'no צור like our God' means no one shapes forms like Him, which is the point of the proof.

phrases.english: What is "there is no rock like our God"?
There is no artist like our God.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains a word in the פסוק just quoted as a proof.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: צור is read as צייר: no one is an artist like הקדוש ברוך הוא.

steps.title: בלתך means no one outlasts You
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בר מנסיא reads 'אין בלתך' as 'אין לבלותך': nothing outlasts הקדוש ברוך הוא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'for there is none besides You' mean? רבי יהודה בר מנסיא said: Do not read it 'there is none besides You', but 'there is none that can outlast You'. A human being is unlike הקדוש ברוך הוא. The things a person makes outlast him, but הקדוש ברוך הוא outlasts the things He makes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains another phrase in חנה's פסוק, using an 'אל תקרי' reading to give it a new meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בלתך is read as לבלותך, from the word for wearing out. A human dies while his work stays behind. הקדוש ברוך הוא lasts forever and sees all His works wear out. This is another way הקדוש ברוך הוא is unlike flesh and blood.

keyTerms.meaning: do not read it as ... but as (a reading that changes the vowels of a word)
to outlast You (to wear You out)

steps.confusionAlert: 'אל תקרי' does not mean the written words of the פסוק are wrong. It adds an extra layer of meaning by reading the word differently.

phrases.english: What is "for there is none besides You"?
Rabbi Yehuda bar Menasya said:
Do not read "for there is none besides You,"
but rather "there is none to outlast You."
For not like the way of the Holy One, Blessed be He,
is the way of flesh and blood:
The way of flesh and blood:
the work of his hands outlasts him,
but the Holy One, Blessed be He, outlasts His works.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״כִּי אֵין בִּלְתֶּךָ״? אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בַּר מְנַסְיָא: אַל תִּקְרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second key phrase in חנה's פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Read 'אין לבלותך': nothing outlasts הקדוש ברוך הוא, while human works outlast their makers.

steps.title: The questioner clarifies his real question
steps.stepSummary: The questioner says he did not mean the meaning of the words. He wanted to know what the five 'ברכי נפשי' correspond to.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what I meant to ask you: these five times 'ברכי נפשי', to what did דוד say them?
steps.whatsHappening: The questioner says the answer missed his point and restates his question more exactly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer explained what one פסוק means. The questioner was really asking about the pattern: דוד says 'ברכי נפשי' five times, so what do those five match? This sets up a new answer.

keyTerms.meaning: this is what I was saying to you (what I really meant)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, אֲנָא הָכִי קָא אָמֵינָא לָךְ:
phrases.english: He said to him: This is what I was saying to you:
these five "Bless, my soul"
corresponding to whom did David say them?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, אֲנָא הָכִי קָא אָמֵינָא לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets aside the previous answer as not addressing the question and makes the question sharper.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What do the five times דוד said 'ברכי נפשי' correspond to?

steps.title: The five ברכי נפשי match הקדוש ברוך הוא and the soul
steps.stepSummary: דוד said the five 'ברכי נפשי' to match הקדוש ברוך הוא and the soul.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said them only about הקדוש ברוך הוא and about the soul.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer gives the key idea: the five 'ברכי נפשי' compare the soul to הקדוש ברוך הוא. The details of the five comparisons come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The soul ('נפשי') blessing הקדוש ברוך הוא is not random. The soul is like הקדוש ברוך הוא in certain ways, so it is fitting for the soul to praise Him. This step opens a list that the גמרא will spell out right after.
steps.whatToRemember: The second approach to 'ברכי נפשי': the five times match the ways the soul is like הקדוש ברוך הוא, so the soul is the right one to praise Him.

phrases.english: He said them only
corresponding to the Holy One, Blessed be He,
and corresponding to the soul.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא אֲמָרָן אֶלָּא כְּנֶגֶד הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא וּכְנֶגֶד נְשָׁמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the clarified question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The five 'ברכי נפשי' match הקדוש ברוך הוא and the soul, which are compared to each other.

steps.title: Five ways the soul is like God
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא lists five ways the נשמה resembles הקדוש ברוך הוא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as הקדוש ברוך הוא fills the world, the soul fills the body. He sees and is not seen, and so does the soul. He feeds the whole world, and the soul feeds the whole body. He is pure, and the soul is pure. He dwells in the most inner rooms, and so does the soul.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the five matching points it promised in the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each line starts with 'מה' (just as) for הקדוש ברוך הוא and 'אף' (so too) for the soul. These five matches explain the five times דוד said 'ברכי נפשי'.

keyTerms.meaning: The innermost rooms, a hidden place

phrases.aramaic: מָה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מָלֵא כָּל הָעוֹלָם —
phrases.english: Just as the Holy One, Blessed be He, fills the whole world,

phrases.aramaic: אַף נְשָׁמָה מְלֵאָה אֶת כָּל הַגּוּף.
phrases.english: so too the soul fills the whole body.

phrases.aramaic: מָה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא רוֹאֶה וְאֵינוֹ נִרְאֶה —
phrases.english: Just as the Holy One, Blessed be He, sees but is not seen,
so too the soul sees but is not seen.

phrases.aramaic: מָה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא זָן אֶת כָּל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ —
phrases.english: Just as the Holy One, Blessed be He, feeds the entire world,

phrases.aramaic: אַף נְשָׁמָה זָנָה אֶת כָּל הַגּוּף.
phrases.english: so too the soul feeds the whole body.
Just as the Holy One, Blessed be He, is pure,
so too the soul is pure.

phrases.aramaic: מָה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא יוֹשֵׁב בְּחַדְרֵי חֲדָרִים —
phrases.english: Just as the Holy One, Blessed be He, dwells in the innermost rooms,
so too the soul dwells in the innermost rooms.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מָלֵא כָּל הָעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the five matches promised in step 34.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The soul matches הקדוש ברוך הוא in five ways: it fills, sees unseen, feeds, is pure, and is hidden.

steps.title: The soul should praise God
steps.stepSummary: Since the soul has these five traits, it should praise the One Who has them too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the one that has these five things come and praise the One Who has these five things.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up the explanation of the five 'ברכי נפשי'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The five matches are not just a comparison. They are the reason the soul is the right one to praise הקדוש ברוך הוא: like praises like.
steps.whatToRemember: דוד said 'ברכי נפשי' five times because the soul is like הקדוש ברוך הוא in five ways, so it is fitting for the soul to praise Him.

phrases.aramaic: יָבֹא מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ חֲמִשָּׁה דְבָרִים הַלָּלוּ
phrases.english: Let the one who has these five things come

phrases.aramaic: וִישַׁבֵּחַ לְמִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ חֲמִשָּׁה דְבָרִים הַלָּלוּ.
phrases.english: and praise the One Who has these five things.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָבֹא מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ חֲמִשָּׁה דְבָרִים הַלָּלוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the five matches in step 35.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The soul, which shares five traits with הקדוש ברוך הוא, is the right one to praise Him.

steps.title: God knows how to make peace between two צדיקים
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא reads a פסוק in קהלת as praising הקדוש ברוך הוא for making a compromise between חזקיהו and ישעיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא said: What does 'Who is like the wise one, and who knows the meaning of a thing' mean? Who is like הקדוש ברוך הוא, Who knows how to make a compromise between two צדיקים, חזקיהו and ישעיהו.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. רב המנונא explains a פסוק, and this sets up the story that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads the word 'פשר' (meaning) as 'פשרה' (compromise). The 'wise one' is הקדוש ברוך הוא. The next steps tell the argument He settled.

phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna said: What is the meaning of what is written:
"Who is like the wise one, and who knows the meaning of a thing"?
Who is like the Holy One, Blessed be He,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁיּוֹדֵעַ לַעֲשׂוֹת פְּשָׁרָה בֵּין שְׁנֵי צַדִּיקִים,
phrases.english: Who knows how to make a compromise between two righteous people,
phrases.notes: He hears the word פשר in the פסוק as פשרה, a compromise.

phrases.english: between Hezekiah and Isaiah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching, unrelated to the 'ברכי נפשי' discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'wise one' of קהלת 8:1 is הקדוש ברוך הוא, Who made a compromise between חזקיהו and ישעיהו.

steps.title: חזקיהו says the נביא should come to the king
steps.stepSummary: חזקיהו wants ישעיהו to come to him, and proves it from אליהו going to אחאב.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיהו said: Let ישעיהו come to me, because that is what we find with אליהו, who went to אחאב, as it says: 'And אליהו went to appear before אחאב.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells the first side of the argument: חזקיהו's position and his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither man wanted to go to the other. חזקיהו points to a case where a נביא went to a king, so the נביא should come to him.

phrases.english: Hezekiah said: Let Isaiah come to me,
because this is what we find with Elijah,
who went to Ahab,
as it says: "And Elijah went to appear before Ahab."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Describes the first side of the argument mentioned in step 37.
steps.raayaObject: The נביא should go to the king.
steps.raayaSupportSource: אליהו went to king אחאב (מלכים א 18:2).

steps.title: ישעיהו says the king should come to the נביא
steps.stepSummary: ישעיהו wants חזקיהו to come to him, and proves it from יהורם going to אלישע.
steps.simpleTranslation: ישעיהו said: Let חזקיהו come to me, because that is what we find with יהורם בן אחאב, who went to אלישע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells the other side: ישעיהו's position and his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ישעיהו answers with the opposite case, where a king went to a נביא. Now each side has a proof, so there is a deadlock.

keyTerms.meaning: A king of ישראל, son of אחאב

phrases.english: Isaiah said: Let Hezekiah come to me,
because this is what we find with Yehoram son of Ahab,
who went to Elisha.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite position, with a counter-proof to step 38.
steps.raayaObject: The king should go to the נביא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: King יהורם בן אחאב went to the נביא אלישע.

steps.title: God makes חזקיהו sick so ישעיהו visits him
steps.stepSummary: הקדוש ברוך הוא settles the argument: He makes חזקיהו ill and sends ישעיהו to visit the sick.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did הקדוש ברוך הוא do? He brought suffering on חזקיהו and told ישעיהו: Go visit the sick man. As it says: 'In those days חזקיהו became deathly ill, and ישעיהו בן אמוץ the נביא came to him and said: So says ה׳ צבאות: Give orders to your household, for you will die and not live.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the compromise from step 37. ישעיהו now goes to חזקיהו, but for the מצוה of visiting the sick, not because the king summoned him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither side has to give in. ישעיהו comes, as חזקיהו wanted, but only because a sick person cannot travel. The פסוק in ישעיהו shows that he really did come.

keyTerms.meaning: Give final instructions to your household

phrases.english: What did the Holy One, Blessed be He, do?
He brought suffering upon Hezekiah,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר לוֹ לִישַׁעְיָהוּ: לֵךְ וּבַקֵּר אֶת הַחוֹלֶה.
phrases.english: and said to Isaiah: Go and visit the sick man.
As it says: "In those days Hezekiah became deathly ill,

phrases.aramaic: וַיָּבֹא אֵלָיו יְשַׁעְיָהוּ בֶּן אָמוֹץ הַנָּבִיא
phrases.english: and Isaiah son of Amoz the prophet came to him

phrases.aramaic: וַיֹּאמֶר אֵלָיו כֹּה אָמַר ה׳ צְבָאוֹת
phrases.english: and said to him: So says the Lord of Hosts:
Give instructions to your household,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי מֵת אַתָּה וְלֹא תִחְיֶה וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: for you will die and you will not live, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the deadlock between steps 38 and 39.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: By making חזקיהו ill, הקדוש ברוך הוא gave ישעיהו a reason to come: visiting the sick.

steps.title: Why does the verse say both die and not live
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the double phrase 'you will die and not live' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'for you will die and you will not live' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask about the wording of the פסוק it just quoted. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'You will die' and 'you will not live' seem to say the same thing twice. The גמרא wants to know what the extra words add.

phrases.english: What is the meaning of "for you will die and you will not live"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the wording of the פסוק quoted in step 40.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the פסוק says both 'die' and 'not live'.

steps.title: Die in this world, not live in the next
steps.stepSummary: 'You will die' means in this world; 'you will not live' means in עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'You will die' in this world, and 'you will not live' in עולם הבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: each phrase is about a different world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So the words are not repeated for nothing. ישעיהו's message was far harsher than a death sentence: חזקיהו would also lose his share in עולם הבא.

phrases.english: "You will die" in this world,
"and you will not live" in the World to Come.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 41.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Each phrase refers to a different world: death here, and no life in עולם הבא.

steps.title: חזקיהו asks why he deserves this
steps.stepSummary: חזקיהו asks ישעיהו why he is getting such a severe punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Why all this?
steps.whatsHappening: Back in the story, חזקיהו asks what he did to deserve such a harsh decree. This sets up ישעיהו's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Losing עולם הבא is the harshest punishment, so חזקיהו wants to know what sin caused it.

phrases.english: He said to him: Why all this?
phrases.notes: חזקיהו is asking: what did I do to deserve such a harsh punishment?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the harsh decree explained in step 42.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What sin caused such a severe punishment.

steps.title: Because he did not have children
steps.stepSummary: ישעיהו says it is because חזקיהו did not do the מצוה of פריה ורביה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Because you did not engage in having children.
steps.whatsHappening: ישעיהו tells חזקיהו what his sin was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sin is not doing something wrong but failing to do a מצוה: having children. Skipping this מצוה is treated as serious enough to lose עולם הבא.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Because you did not engage in having children.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers חזקיהו's question in step 43.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The punishment is for not doing the מצוה of פריה ורביה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how seriously the מצוה of פריה ורביה is taken: not doing it can cost a person his share in עולם הבא.

steps.title: חזקיהו explains why he had no children
steps.stepSummary: חזקיהו defends himself: through רוח הקודש he saw that his children would not be good.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Because I saw through רוח הקודש that the children who come from me will not be good.
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיהו answers the charge and explains his reason. The story goes on in the next part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חזקיהו does not deny that he skipped the מצוה. He claims a good reason: he did not want to bring bad children into the world. This sets up ישעיהו's reply to that excuse.

keyTerms.meaning: Who are not good, not worthy

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִשּׁוּם דַּחֲזַאי לִי בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ
phrases.english: He said to him: Because I saw through divine inspiration
that children who are not good will come out from me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends against the charge given in step 44.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Justification: admits the fact but gives a reason for it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: חזקיהו simply neglected the מצוה of having children.
steps.terutzMaskana: חזקיהו chose not to have children because רוח הקודש showed him they would not be good.

steps.title: ישעיהו rejects the excuse: do what you are commanded
steps.stepSummary: ישעיהו tells חזקיהו that God's hidden plans are not his business. His job is to keep the מצוה, and God will do what He wants.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Why do you get involved in God's secrets? You should have done what you were commanded, and let God do what is good in His eyes.
steps.whatsHappening: ישעיהו pushes back on חזקיהו's defense from the last step. Seeing through רוח הקודש that his children would be bad does not excuse skipping the מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חזקיהו argued that he knew the future, so he held back. ישעיהו answers that a person's duty is set by the command, not by guesses about how things will turn out. The results belong to God.

keyTerms.meaning: the hidden secrets of God (literally, of the Merciful One)
the Holy One, Blessed be He

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a basic principle: a person must keep a מצוה even if he thinks he can predict a bad outcome.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בַּהֲדֵי כַּבְשֵׁי דְרַחֲמָנָא לְמָה לָךְ?
phrases.english: He said to him: Why do you get involved with the secrets of the Merciful One?
phrases.notes: ישעיהו is the one speaking here.

phrases.english: What you were commanded, you should have done,

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה דְנִיחָא קַמֵּיהּ קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא — לַעֲבֵיד.
phrases.english: and what is pleasing to the Holy One, Blessed be He, let Him do.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges חזקיהו's defense from step 45
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that knowing the future excuses skipping פריה ורביה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Your duty comes from the command, not from predicting results

steps.title: חזקיהו asks to marry ישעיהו's daughter
steps.stepSummary: חזקיהו accepts the point and tries to fix things. He asks for ישעיהו's daughter as a wife, hoping their combined merit will bring good children.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Then give me your daughter now. Maybe my merit and your merit together will make good children come from me.
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיהו stops defending himself and tries to repair the situation. He wants to do the מצוה now, with ישעיהו's daughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His worry was bad children. He hopes that adding ישעיהו's merit can change that outcome. This also suggests the punishment might be cancelled.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הַשְׁתָּא הַב לִי בְּרַתָּךְ,
phrases.english: He said to him: Now give me your daughter;
perhaps my merit and your merit will cause
that good children will come out of me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts ישעיהו's point and offers a fix
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical repair: doing the מצוה now in a way that addresses the fear of bad children
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It is too late, and the children will be bad anyway
steps.terutzMaskana: Combined merit might produce good children, so he can still do the מצוה

steps.title: ישעיהו says the decree is already sealed
steps.stepSummary: ישעיהו turns down the offer: the decree against חזקיהו has already been made.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: A decree has already been decreed against you.
steps.whatsHappening: ישעיהו rejects חזקיהו's plan. He says it is too late to change the sentence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ישעיהו treats the punishment as final, so there is no point in a fix now. This sets up חזקיהו's strong reply in the next steps.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כְּבָר נִגְזְרָה עָלֶיךָ גְּזֵירָה.
phrases.english: He said to him: A decree has already been decreed against you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proposal in step 47
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the marriage offer as a way to change the outcome

steps.title: חזקיהו sends ישעיהו away
steps.stepSummary: חזקיהו refuses to accept that all hope is gone. He tells ישעיהו to finish his prophecy and leave.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Son of אמוץ, finish your prophecy and go out!
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיהו pushes back against ישעיהו's claim that nothing can be done. He ends the conversation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חזקיהו does not deny the prophecy itself. He rejects the idea that the decree cannot change. His reason comes in the next step.

phrases.english: He said to him: Son of Amoz,
finish your prophecy and go out!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers ישעיהו's claim from step 48
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the decree cannot be changed
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Prayer can still help, as explained next

steps.title: A family tradition: never stop praying
steps.stepSummary: חזקיהו backs up his refusal with a tradition from his family: even with a sharp sword on your neck, do not stop asking for mercy.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the tradition I received from my grandfather's house: even if a sharp sword is resting on a person's neck, he should not hold himself back from praying for mercy.
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיהו explains why he will not give up. He quotes a tradition passed down in his family.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ישעיהו said the decree was final. חזקיהו answers that no situation is too far gone for prayer. Even at the last moment, a person should ask for mercy.
steps.whatToRemember: Never give up on תפילה. Even when things look completely lost, a person should still pray for mercy.

phrases.english: So I have received from the house of my father's father:
phrases.notes: חזקיהו is still talking. 'My father's father' means a tradition handed down in his family.

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ חֶרֶב חַדָּה מוּנַּחַת עַל צַוָּארוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם,
phrases.english: even if a sharp sword is resting on a person's neck,
he should not hold himself back from mercy.
phrases.notes: He means praying to God for mercy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for sending ישעיהו away in step 49
steps.raayaObject: That a decree does not end the chance for prayer to help
steps.raayaSupportSource: A family tradition from חזקיהו's ancestors

steps.title: רבי יוחנן and רבי אליעזר teach the same thing from a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds that רבי יוחנן and רבי אליעזר both taught this same rule and supported it with a פסוק from איוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught: רבי יוחנן and רבי אליעזר both said: Even if a sharp sword is resting on a person's neck, he should not hold himself back from praying for mercy, as it says: 'Though He kill me, I will hope in Him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps out of the story to show that אמוראים taught the same idea. It gives a פסוק as the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What was a family tradition in the story now becomes a rule taught by חכמים with a פסוק behind it. איוב says that even if God is about to kill him, he still hopes in God.

keyTerms.meaning: it was also taught (a supporting statement)

steps.whyThisMatters: It turns the lesson of the story into a general teaching about תפילה for everyone.

phrases.english: It was also said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר דְאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan and Rabbi Eliezer both said:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ חֶרֶב חַדָּה מוּנַּחַת עַל צַוָּארוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם,
phrases.english: Even if a sharp sword is resting on a person's neck,
he should not hold himself back from mercy,
as it is said: 'Though He kill me, I will hope in Him.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the tradition of step 50 with אמוראים and a פסוק
steps.raayaObject: The rule that one should never stop praying for mercy
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן and רבי אליעזר, based on איוב 13:15
